source.title: The Constitution of India
source.authority: Government of India, Ministry of Law and Justice, Legislative Department

rules: Use the Constitution of India as the primary constitutional source wherever the topic is directly covered by the constitutional text.
Do not invent Article numbers, Parts, Schedules, constitutional powers, constitutional procedures or constitutional institutions.
If a topic is conceptual and has no single constitutional provision, identify it as conceptual rather than attaching an unrelated Article.
Distinguish clearly between the constitutional text, ordinary legislation, judicial interpretation, historical fact and general democratic explanation.
Where the Constitution alone is insufficient, mark the day as requiring an additional authoritative source.
Historical topics must not be generated from the constitutional text alone.
Statutory topics must not be presented as though the Constitution itself contains the complete statutory rule.
Judicial doctrines must not be presented as though they are literal wording of an Article unless the constitutional text actually says so.
The generator must not silently fill a source gap with general knowledge.
The listed sources are factual boundaries for generation.

source_types.constitutional: The Constitution itself is the principal authoritative source for the topic.
source_types.conceptual: The topic explains a constitutional concept without relying on one specific Article.
source_types.historical: The topic requires authoritative historical material in addition to the Constitution.
source_types.statutory: The topic requires an Act, rules or another authoritative legal source in addition to the Constitution.
source_types.judicial: The topic requires authoritative judicial interpretation in addition to the constitutional text.
source_types.mixed: The topic requires more than one type of authoritative source.
